newsitem.title: JAPAN: New cash JGB benchmark switch likely next week.
newsitem.headline: New cash JGB benchmark switch likely next week.

text.p: The 190th 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) is likely to replace the 182nd issue as the key cash JGB benchmark early next week, market sources said on Friday.
The 182nd issue has been the benchmark cash JGB since late February 1996.

The market practice is to adopt the 10-year JGB with the largest turnover as the benchmark issue, said Takeshi Naito, assistant general manager for the market intelligence unit at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd's bond department.
"The cash JGB issue with the greatest turnover becomes the benchmark, but there is no clear rule about when a benchmark shift becomes official," Naito said.
Turnover of the 190th JGB will probably have to exceed that of the 182nd JGB for at least several days in order for the market to consider it the new benchmark, Naito said.

According to the Japan Bond Trading Co Ltd (JBTC), the largest inter-dealer broker in Japan, turnover of the 190th JGB totalled 290 lots by midday on Friday, higher than the 182nd's turnover of 160 contracts.
But JGB turnover in general, however, was too small in the morning to say for certain whether the market was ready to immediately adopt the 190th as the new benchmark, a JBTC official said.
"Combined turnover of cash JGBs traded through JBTC was only 940 lots this morning... I think the market trend will become clear sometime early next week," the official said.
The 190th JGB has become the heir apparent to the 182nd benchmark JGB because of its large liquidity, the JBTC official said.

Two tranches of 190th JGBs were issued in October and November 1996, with coupon rates of 2.9 percent, and beginning with the October and November 190th JGBs traded on Friday and due for delivery on June 20, they will be combined into one tranche.
